editorial.headline: Sterile Medical Supplies and Dental Materials Manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32509 covers the making of specialised medical, dental, and surgical-use supplies, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32509 sits in the practical, material side of health care: the manufacturing of medical and dental equipment, plus other supporting supplies used in clinical and surgical settings. The scope is concrete rather than abstract. It includes sterile surgical cloth and thread, tissue paper, personal protective masks such as FFP2, FFP3, and surgical masks, surgical drapes, surgical gowns, head covers, and wound dressings for health services. It also reaches into dental and orthopaedic materials: dental cement and fillings, dental wax, other dental plaster preparations, and bone reconstruction cement.

That makes this a manufacturing activity for businesses producing physical inputs used by clinics, hospitals, surgery rooms, dental practices, and health-service providers. The common thread is not retail, distribution, or professional medical service; it is the making of these goods. A company registering this code should be able to describe its activity as production of the listed medical, surgical, dental, or related health-care supplies, not merely trading them or using them as part of another service.

The scale picture is unusually broad in the slim record. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses. That matters because the code is not framed only for large industrial operators; the record recognises every listed business scale. At the same time, the nature of the goods is specialised. Sterility, protective use, surgical use, dental preparation, and reconstruction materials all point to a sector where the registered activity should be stated with care and matched closely to what the company actually manufactures.

Nationally, the investment signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali picture is also not blocked in this record. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this record marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest reading is straightforward: this activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and the slim record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
